criteria.text: Identifies that the basket in SPA Section 9.4 ($200,000) operates as a deductible (Seller liable only for the excess), not a tipping basket, and explains that this is less favourable to the Buyer.

Identifies that the core platform was developed by contractor Northgate Pharma plc without a written IP assignment, so the Company may not own it, and recommends obtaining a confirmatory assignment as a condition to Closing.

Identifies that the Oakhurst Media Ltd contract (Clause 14.2) allows termination on a change of control without consent, that the disclosure against Warranty 6.3 says there is no such provision, and that consent should be obtained as a condition to Closing.
Identifies that the 5-year SPA non-compete may be unenforceable as wider than reasonably necessary and is inconsistent with the 18-month restriction in the Founder's employment agreement.
Calculates the working capital shortfall as $620,000 and the adjusted Purchase Price as $39,380,000, identifying that the Seller's funds flow figure of $38,760,000 is wrong.
Flags that the disclosure letter is inconsistent with the material contract on change of control.
Lists a confirmatory IP assignment from Northgate Pharma plc as a required third-party action not yet obtained.
Gives a pinpoint citation (document name and section/clause number) for every issue or finding.
